full_judgment: 3. This petitioner as defendant No. 1 has been contesting the suit by filing written statement stating, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable, that the suit is barred by the principle of res-judicata. The further case of the petitioner is that the opposite party No. 5 while owning and possessing the suit property entered into an agreement with petitioner on 1-1-1969 to sell the same and subsequently the petitioner got the specific performance of the said contract in the Title Suit No. 3(16 of 1969 and got the Kabala Deed No. 15892 dated 6-10-1983 registered through Court vide Title Execution Case No. 21 of 1981 and obtained possession of the suit property (in part) vide Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1984 (renumbered on transfer) and was waiting for obtaining possession of the rest of the suit property. It is further asserted that the plaintiff opposite parties preferred Title Appeal No. 92 of 1980 against the aforesaid judgment and decree which on transfer being dismissed by the 5th Additional District Judge, Dhaka Civil Revision No. 1146 of 1991 was preferred before this court by the opposite party Nos. 1-5 which however was discharged for default on 26-2-1982 and subsequently a review petition thereon also being discharged Civil Appeal No. 117 of 1989 was preferred before the Appellate Division of this court which was also dismissed on 31-3-1993. It is further stated in the written statement that the plaintiff opposite party No. 5 also filed Civil Revision No. 695 of 1989 against the party for delivery of possession of the suit land vide Execution Case No. 3 of 1984 and the Rule of that Civil Revision was also discharged 13-4-1988. It is asserted by the defendant petitioner in the written statement that being unsuccessful in the aforesaid case the plaintiff opposite party Nos. 1-4 filed Title Suit No. 172 of 1984 before the Assistant Judge, Keraniganj challenging the petitioners' aforesaid Sale Deed which was dismissed for default on 11-2-1985. Thereafter they filed another title suit being Title Suit No. 826 of 1985 before the 2nd Sub-Judge, Dhaka, for declaration of their title in the suit land and ultimately withdrew the suit to sue afresh subsequently and thereafter filed the instant Title Suit No. 8 of 1989.
